note: Measured but not yet bound to a ledger fact. An entry here is a claim the instrument can support and the ledger does not yet assert. `elohim --promote ID:TOL` binds one.

measurements.claim: a check establishes the claim it verifies, not merely references its scope
measurements.origin: NOT MEASURED, and the shipped fixture proved it is not the same test. A claim reading 'the contract does not carry the marker' had a check that grepped for the contract HEADER; with the marker present the check still exited 0 and the claim was reported reproduced. Measured directly: exit=0 on a contract carrying the marker. The scope string WAS in the argv, so the off-scope test could not see it.
measurements.why_not_bound: deciding whether a check ESTABLISHES its claim is a judgement about meaning, and a judgement step in the measurement path is the thing this design exists to avoid. Recorded as a limit in references/limits.md and pinned by a negative control rather than bound as a number.

measurements.claim: the share of a run's claims that are reproduced by the check they name
measurements.origin: 2 of 2 claims in the pinned corpus, which is correct by construction
measurements.why_not_bound: a fraction over a corpus built to be correct measures the fixture, not any run. There is no population of real agent claims in this repository to compute a rate over, and a number that reads as a general rate would be the exact overclaim this skill exists to catch.

measurements.claim: the claims file is derived from what the run actually said, rather than written by the run being judged
measurements.why_not_bound: DECIDED, not merely deferred. jev 0.6.2 ranked it last of three at probability 0.12, below the 0.78 working threshold, so the owner chose `both`: ship the agent-written path now and build transcript extraction as a SEPARATE LATER SKILL that feeds this one a file. The reasoning behind splitting it: extraction from prose has no published reliable method, a deterministic extractor under-extracts, and an LLM extractor would put a judgement step inside the measurement path, which is the one thing this design forbids -- so folding it in would make the gate worse than the thing it gates. Isolating it keeps the research question from blocking a working gate, at the cost of two skills, and the later skill inherits the same AUROC 0.65 ceiling on its own accuracy.
measurements.note_on_the_shape_linter: The `both` option was described as shipping a deterministic shape linter alongside the agent-written path. MEASURED: it already ships. the_unverifiable_claim, the_green_check_that_checked_nothing and the_decorative_check run in applied mode, not only on the pinned fixture -- fed a deliberately badly-shaped file (one claim with no check, one evidenced by `true`, one whose `asserts` appears nowhere in its argv), all three went red and claims_reproduced was 0. No new linter was written, because writing one would have been a second implementation of a gate that already fires.

measurements.claim: the rate at which a self-authored claims file is detected as self-authored
measurements.why_not_bound: ELOHIM_CLAIM_AUTHOR catches a run that declares itself. A run that does not set it, or sets the wrong value, is not detectable from inside the measured process. The measured size of the general problem is the 32% catch rate in SLEIGHT-Bench, which is a different measurement and must not be quoted as this instrument's rate.

measurements.claim: a claim verified today still holds months later
measurements.origin: NOT MEASURED, and there is no time dimension in v1
measurements.why_not_bound: the seal deliberately excludes the generated timestamp so nothing can be pinned to when a run happened. Auditing whether a claim decayed is decision-decay's territory, and building it here would ship a second skill's job inside the first one's name.
